## TL;DR

Round two addresses the review findings that kept project-owned remote checks from being usable. Settings now edits the command and required tools, probes match the execution shell and reject old copied runner scripts, and the custom Docker path keeps its named container and caches. The docs describe Linux/macOS native setup, Docker setup, and an Android/Gradle example. A Tiao-shaped fixture runs a command from a different project root through the native validator and verifies shell chaining, logs, and a returned artifact. The required RepoOS check passed on the ThinkPad runner. No Android SDK or Tiao checkout was available, so there is no claim of a live Gradle/device run.

## Work and rationale

The review correctly noted that schema registration alone did not make the settings available. I added `remoteValidation.command` and `remoteValidation.requiredTools` to the rendered Remote validation section. The command gets a text input; required tools use comma-separated text and save as a string array. Tests cover both settings discovery and the save payload.

For Docker custom commands, the runner now starts the actual gate as `--name "$CONTAINER"`. The existing watchdog, hang-kill path, prefix reaper, and slot release all rely on that name to identify and control the container. The checkout and artifacts remain mounted at their existing paths. A named runner volume persists HOME and package caches across disposable runs, with Gradle, npm, Bun, and RepoOS cache variables directed into it. Browser-capture environment is forwarded. Browser-step offload remains available for RepoOS projects whose command builds `dist/cli/index.js`; if requested without that output, the runner records an actionable failure. Native runs naturally retain package caches under the SSH user's home.

The probe selects the user-installed validator path first, then falls back to `/opt/repoos/validate.sh`, matching dispatch. It checks the artifact-argument contract and prints independent mirror and project-command capability markers. A configured command requires the latter; older copied scripts fail the probe with an update instruction rather than silently running the Bun sequence. Native tool checks run in a login shell with the Homebrew PATH prefix used at execution. Docker image checks use a login shell as well. Stock gates continue to require Bun even when `requiredTools` is set; a custom command checks the declared tools plus host Git.

Documentation now describes the maintained native Linux and macOS path, per-host Docker setup, and which setup steps require sudo. The Android/Gradle example declares `java`, `gradle`, and `node`, shows a project script that writes a report under `REPOOS_ARTIFACTS_DIR`, and explains user-level tool installation. Outdated macOS-only and fixed-Bun descriptions were corrected. The existing engineer-session follow-up order remains: settle ADR acceptance, implement load-aware remote sessions, then do CLI authentication and live proof.

## Approaches tried

The first focused pass caught stale probe tests that asserted the old shell-escaped command string and a runner-script test that assumed one working directory. I changed those tests to check the required tool names and capability markers and to locate the repository by searching upward for the script.

The Settings save test then showed the settings template still rendered only selects and switches. I added string and array editors and verified both values save correctly.

I expanded the Tiao-shaped fixture to include shell chaining. That exposed that the native validator expanded the configured command without asking the login shell to parse its operators. It now evaluates the configured command text inside `bash -lc`. The fixture runs an independent temporary project with its own config, command, git bundle, and artifact file; it asserts both the chained output and collected logs/artifact.

The first required check built successfully but exposed two outdated assertions around the runner dispatcher: one expected a literal `/opt` command, and another extracted `$5` from that legacy command shape. I updated them to verify the user-level-first selection, `/opt` fallback, and preserved home-relative mirror argument. The focused remote-validation suite then passed all 58 tests.

## Challenges and blockers

The final `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed using ThinkPad: build and Vue typecheck, all 570 selected test files (8,113 passed, one skipped), rendered contrast audit, and UI smoke. The local follow-up guards, contrast audit, UI smoke, and user-docs build passed too. The task branch's stock gate was exercised through the real pool host. The custom-command behavior was exercised through the native validator script with a separate Tiao-shaped root, but not through a live custom-command SSH dispatch to ThinkPad, bee, or mini. No Tiao checkout, Android SDK, or device was available for a true Gradle run.

## Key learnings

A config key is not usable until the Settings page routes it and renders an editor for its type. Prerequisite probes must test the environment the execution shell sees, including login initialization and PATH changes. Capability handshakes should protect command semantics from old copied runner scripts, not just optimize bundle transport. Finally, named containers and persistent cache mounts are part of the concurrency and recovery contract: a custom check must preserve those lifecycle guarantees while replacing the gate command.
